reading: Each isolated pixel grows into the full square ring, centred on the grid centre, that passes through it (ring index = Chebyshev distance of the pixel from the centre); the rings together cover the whole grid.

slots.seeds: the isolated non-background pixels (one per ring distance)
slots.centre: the grid centre cell (odd square grid)
slots.ring: all cells at the seed's Chebyshev distance from the centre

why: the output cell at Chebyshev distance r from the centre has the colour of the unique input pixel at distance r
invariants: the seed pixels keep their colour

reading: Shapes with a hole (hollow rectangles) slide straight up and solid plus/cross shapes slide straight down, each until it hits the grid border or another shape already stacked there.

slots.direction: up if the object encloses a background hole, down if it has no hole
slots.stop: grid border or another object (stack in order of travel)

why: every holed object ends touching the top border or a holed object above it; every cross ends touching the bottom border or a cross below it; columns and shapes are kept

reading: Every 2-cell that has no orthogonal (4-neighbour) non-background neighbour becomes 1; diagonal contact does not count.

new_rows.name: iso4
new_rows.datalog:
has4(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, D).
has4(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, D).
iso4(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !has4(Y, X).

why: exactly the non-background cells with no 4-neighbour of non-background colour change, 2 -> 1

reading: Several equal-size square boxes framed in 8 with a 2/8 interior pattern lie in noisy 1/8 background; all boxes share one interior pattern except one, and the output is that odd box cut out (frame included).

slots.candidates: the square 8-framed boxes containing 2s (same size within a grid; stray 8 noise pixels may touch them)
slots.criterion: the box whose interior pattern (translation only) differs from all the others
slots.output: that box's full extent, frame included

why: the output equals the one box whose interior 2-pattern occurs only once among the boxes

reading: Four same-colour corner pixels mark a rectangle; the cells strictly inside it are filled with 2.

new_rows.name: rect_inside
new_rows.datalog: rect_inside(Y, X) :- cell(Y1, X1, C), cell(Y1, X2, C), cell(Y2, X1, C), cell(Y2, X2, C), px(Y, X, D), Y > Y1, Y < Y2, X > X1, X < X2.

why: every cell strictly between the rows and columns of a 4-corner rectangle becomes 2; nothing else changes
invariants: all cells outside the rectangle interiors

reading: A 5-separated half shows a small line lattice (vertical and horizontal coloured lines with a fixed crossing precedence); the other half has 4-markers on its borders giving line positions. The output is the marker half with the lattice redrawn: verticals at the marked columns, horizontals at the marked rows, colours in the same order and the same line on top at crossings.

slots.source: the lattice panel (visible part beside the 5 separator/block)
slots.target: the panel holding the 4-markers; output has its size
slots.positions: columns marked by 4s on top/bottom edge, rows marked by 4s on left/right edge
slots.colours: k-th vertical / horizontal line colour of the lattice, in order
slots.precedence: whichever orientation is on top at crossings in the lattice

why: each output column with an edge marker is a full line of the matching lattice colour, each marked row likewise, with the lattice's crossing rule; all else 0

reading: The input splits into two equal halves: a colour pattern and a mask drawn in 8. The output is the Kronecker product: each coloured cell of the pattern becomes a copy of the mask in that colour, each 0 cell an empty block.

slots.block: mask recoloured with the pattern cell's colour, or empty for 0

why: output block (i,j) = mask with 8 replaced by pattern[i][j] (all 0 if pattern[i][j] = 0)
invariants: mask shape in every non-empty block

reading: A legend panel (8 background) pairs small 3x3 shapes with colours. Each 5x5 box carrying a 1-pattern on 2 becomes solid in the colour whose legend shape matches the pattern; each solid-colour box becomes the 2 box with that colour's legend shape drawn in 1.

slots.pattern->colour: box with 1s on 2: fill solid with the colour whose shape equals the 1-pattern
slots.colour->pattern: solid box of colour c: 2 border/background with c's legend shape in 1 in the 3x3 interior

why: every box is swapped between its pattern form and its colour form through the legend

reading: Each domino (two orthogonally adjacent 2s) gets a ring of 3 around it on the surrounding background cells; single 2s are untouched.

new_rows.name: domino_halo
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dom(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 2, off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2).
dom(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 2, off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2).
domino_halo(Y, X) :- dom(Y0, X0), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).

why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a 2-cell orthogonal domino become 3

reading: A key row gives a colour sequence; each diagonal band of 5 is a stack of WxW squares stepping one cell diagonally from its top end. The squares are painted in order with the key colours cycling, later squares overwriting earlier ones, so the band shows nested L-strokes and ends in a solid square.
verb: paint diagonal band with cycling key

slots.key: the multi-colour 1-row strip, read left to right
slots.band: each 5-object: union of WxW squares shifted (1,+-1) per step, starting at its top row (W = width of its top row)
slots.order: square k+1 painted over square k

why: every 5 cell takes the colour of the last (highest k) band square containing it; nothing else changes
